review_evidence: Original Zidd-authored English content; NCERT structural alignment reviewed against the source map
Focused extended-remediation self-review: three fresh authored revision levels per level, three disjoint assessment forms, skill coverage, deterministic grading, and key privacy PASS
title: Papa's Spectacles
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Follow the search clues
levels.focus: track an object through details and evidence
levels.teaching_goal: Locate explicit story details and combine clues to decide where a missing object is likely to be.

guided_check.teaching_block: A careful reader links an object to the action and place named with it. Start with the clearest stated location.
guided_check.passage: Papa took off his spectacles to polish a misty lens and set them beside the green gardening diary. A phone call then drew him into the hall.
guided_check.prompt: Where did Papa place his spectacles before the phone call?
options: beside the green gardening diary
inside his shirt pocket
under the hall rug
on the telephone table
accepted_answers: beside the green gardening diary
beside the gardening diary
next to the green diary

bridge.teaching_block: Search actions reveal a character's goal. Notice which missing object connects all the places being checked.
bridge.passage: Back in the room, Papa checked the windowsill, opened the pencil drawer, and shook out the newspaper. He kept asking who had moved his glasses.
bridge.prompt: Which object is Papa trying to find?
options: his spectacles
a pencil
the newspaper
a window key
accepted_answers: his spectacles
spectacles
his glasses
glasses

masterclass.teaching_block: Strong inferences join two clues: where an object was last used and what remains in that place.
masterclass.passage: Ritu remembers that Papa wore his spectacles while reading a seed packet. She now sees the folded packet on the balcony table and a clean patch in the dust beside it.
masterclass.prompt: Explain why the balcony table is a sensible next place to check.

concept_slots.description: Connects the spectacles with reading the seed packet.
any_of: used his glasses to read the seed packet
last used the spectacles for the packet

concept_slots.description: Uses the packet or clean dust mark as evidence for checking the table.
any_of: packet is on the balcony table
clean patch is beside the packet
dust mark may show where the glasses rested

revision_level_1.teaching_block: Let's practise with one direct placement clue. Ask three questions: what was moved, where was it put, and what happened next?
revision_level_1.passage: Before choir practice, Ana removed her silver hair clip and tucked it into the small pocket of her music folder. When practice ended, she searched the piano bench.
revision_level_1.prompt: Use the placement clue: where should Ana look first?
options: in the small pocket of her music folder
under the piano bench
inside the songbook cupboard
beside the water cooler
accepted_answers: in the small pocket of her music folder
in her music folder pocket
the small pocket of the music folder

revision_level_2.teaching_block: Now combine a last-use clue with a mark left in that place. Both details should point to the same sensible search location.
revision_level_2.passage: Rohan used a magnifying glass to study a leaf at the science window. The leaf tray is still there, and an empty circular mark shows in the dust beside it.
revision_level_2.prompt: Which pair of details makes the science window a useful place to check?
options: Rohan used the glass there, and a circular dust mark remains beside the leaf tray.
The window is made of glass, and the classroom has a door.
The leaf is green, and Rohan enjoys science lessons.
The tray can be carried, and the shelf is newly painted.
accepted_answers: Rohan used the glass there, and a circular dust mark remains beside the leaf tray.
he used it at the window and the dust mark is beside the tray
the last-use clue and circular mark both point to the science window

revision_level_3.teaching_block: Try a supported retrace. Name the first place to check, then explain the final action that puts the object there.
revision_level_3.passage: During pottery club, Ms Das removed her ring before kneading clay and placed it in a lidded bead cup on the supply shelf. Later, she checked the sink.
revision_level_3.prompt: Name the first place to check and connect it to Ms Das's last action.

concept_slots.description: Names the lidded bead cup on the supply shelf as the first place to check.
any_of: bead cup on the supply shelf

concept_slots.description: Explains that Ms Das put the ring there before kneading clay.
any_of: placed the ring in the cup
put it there before kneading clay
removed her ring and placed it in the bead cup
the cup was the last place she put the ring

forbidden_phrases: the sink is the only clue
the ring was never placed anywhere

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the last clear action as evidence. Name both the place to check and the clue that leads there.
independent_check.passage: At the library, Dev removed his membership card to copy its number and slipped it between the pages of a blue atlas. At checkout, he searched every pocket.
independent_check.prompt: Where should Dev look first, and which detail supports your answer?

concept_slots.description: Names the blue atlas or its pages as the first place to look.
Explains that Dev slipped the card there after copying its number.
any_of: he slipped the card between its pages
put it in the atlas after copying the number
the last place he placed it was the atlas
he tucked it between the pages

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the same evidence method to a new setting: retrace the final action before the object went missing.
transfer_check.passage: Before cricket practice, the captain unclipped a silver whistle to tie his shoelace and placed it on the lowest bench. Later, he searched the kit bag for it.
transfer_check.prompt: What is the most useful place to check, and why?

concept_slots.description: Names the lowest bench as the useful place to check.
Explains that the captain placed the whistle there while tying his lace.
any_of: put it on the bench to tie his shoelace
unclipped it and set it on the bench

forbidden_phrases: the kit bag is the only clue

levels.title: Explain the funny mistake
levels.focus: infer why a search becomes humorous
levels.teaching_goal: Use visible evidence to explain a character's mistaken belief and the humour it creates.

guided_check.teaching_block: A scene can be funny when the reader notices something that the searching character has missed.
guided_check.passage: Papa pushed his spectacles above his eyebrows while wiping sweat. Minutes later, he asked everyone to help him find them.
options: He is searching for something he is already wearing.
He has decided not to read today.
The family has hidden every pair of spectacles.
The spectacles have fallen outside the house.
accepted_answers: He is searching for something he is already wearing.
the spectacles are already above his eyebrows
his glasses are already on his head

bridge.teaching_block: To explain the mistake, contrast what the person believes with what another character can see.
bridge.passage: Naman walked from room to room looking for his cap. His sister noticed the cap hanging from his backpack strap.
bridge.prompt: Why could Naman's sister solve the problem quickly?
options: She could see the cap attached to his backpack.
She owned an identical cap in her room.
She had searched the whole neighbourhood.
She remembered buying the backpack.
accepted_answers: She could see the cap attached to his backpack.
the cap was hanging from his backpack
she noticed it on the backpack strap

masterclass.teaching_block: An evidence-backed reason names the overlooked clue and connects it to the character's unnecessary search.
masterclass.passage: Papa says the print has suddenly become blurry, yet he never checks the top of his head. Meera notices one arm of the spectacles just above his ear.
masterclass.prompt: Give an evidence-backed reason Meera smiles before telling Papa where to look.

concept_slots.description: Uses the spectacle arm above Papa's ear as evidence.
any_of: spectacle arm is above his ear
Meera can see the glasses on his head
one arm of the spectacles is visible
spectacles are resting above his ear

concept_slots.description: Explains that Papa is searching even though he is already wearing them.
any_of: he is looking for glasses he is wearing
he has forgotten they are on his head
he thinks they are missing when they are not

revision_level_1.teaching_block: Begin by separating belief from evidence: the character believes an object is missing, but the reader can already see it.
revision_level_1.passage: Kabir called for help finding his library token while the token dangled from the lanyard around his neck.
options: The token is already hanging around his neck.
The library has closed for the day.
His friend owns a different token.
The lanyard is a bright colour.
accepted_answers: The token is already hanging around his neck.
the token is on the lanyard around his neck
he is wearing the token he wants to find

revision_level_2.teaching_block: Next, build the reason with because: name the unnecessary search and the action proving the object is already there.
revision_level_2.passage: Nandita searched the sofa for the television remote while lowering the volume with that remote in her left hand.
revision_level_2.prompt: Which answer best explains Nandita's mistake?
options: Her search is unnecessary because she is already using the remote.
She should search faster because the sofa is large.
The volume is low because the remote has disappeared.
Her left hand is empty because the remote is on the sofa.
accepted_answers: Her search is unnecessary because she is already using the remote.
she is looking for the remote while holding and using it
the remote is already in her left hand

revision_level_3.teaching_block: Now explain the humour in your own words. Use one visible clue and connect it directly to the mistaken request.
revision_level_3.passage: At a shop counter, Mr Roy asked the cashier to help find his wallet. The cashier could see a receipt sticking out of the wallet tucked under Mr Roy's arm.
revision_level_3.prompt: Explain why the cashier can point instead of starting a search.

concept_slots.description: Uses the visible wallet or receipt under Mr Roy's arm as evidence.
any_of: receipt is sticking out of the wallet
wallet is tucked under Mr Roy's arm

concept_slots.description: Explains that the wallet is not actually missing, so pointing is enough.
any_of: pointing shows him the overlooked wallet

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain the misunderstanding in a fresh scene by naming the object and the action that reveals it.
independent_check.passage: Ishita searched her desk for a pencil while tapping that same pencil against her notebook as she thought.
independent_check.prompt: Explain Ishita's mistake and why the moment could make a friend smile.

concept_slots.description: States that Ishita is holding or tapping the pencil.
any_of: the same pencil is against her notebook

concept_slots.description: Explains that she searches for an object she already has.
any_of: searching for something she already has
does not realise she is holding it

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the same reasoning to a workplace scene. State what the person overlooks and why another person need not search.
transfer_check.passage: A baker asked an apprentice to find the measuring spoon while using that spoon to stir a bowl of icing.
transfer_check.prompt: Why would the apprentice point to the bowl instead of beginning a search?

concept_slots.description: States that the baker is already using the measuring spoon.
any_of: baker is using the measuring spoon
measuring spoon is already in the bowl
the spoon is in the baker's hand

concept_slots.description: Explains that pointing reveals the overlooked object, so no search is needed.
any_of: the apprentice can show the baker
it has not actually gone missing

forbidden_phrases: the apprentice must search every shelf
the spoon is in another room

levels.title: Read search words in context
levels.focus: understand spectacles, glanced, and related looking words
levels.teaching_goal: Use surrounding actions and time clues to understand and use words connected with seeing and searching.

guided_check.teaching_block: Spectacles are eyeglasses worn to make letters or objects easier to see.
guided_check.passage: Mr Sen put on his spectacles before reading the tiny number printed on a medicine box.
guided_check.prompt: What are spectacles in this sentence?
options: eyeglasses
medicine boxes
printed numbers
reading lamps
accepted_answers: eyeglasses
glasses
a pair of glasses

bridge.teaching_block: Glanced means looked quickly. A brief action after the look is often the clue.
bridge.passage: Farah glanced at the kitchen timer and immediately returned to rolling the dough.
options: looked quickly
watched for an hour
covered completely
carried away
accepted_answers: looked quickly
took a quick look
looked for a moment

masterclass.teaching_block: Compare nearby actions to separate a quick glance from a careful peer into a difficult space.
masterclass.passage: From the doorway, Asha glanced at the clock for a second. At the cupboard, she peered into the dark top shelf until a shape became clear.
masterclass.prompt: Explain how glanced and peered describe different kinds of looking.

concept_slots.description: Explains that glanced describes a quick look at the clock.
Explains that peered describes looking carefully into the dark shelf.
any_of: looked closely into the dark shelf
tried hard to see the shape
kept looking until it became clear

forbidden_phrases: both words mean closing the eyes

revision_level_1.teaching_block: Use the difficulty clue around a looking word. When something is dim or hard to see, peered usually means looked closely and carefully.
revision_level_1.passage: The trail map had faded in the rain, so Rina held it near the lantern and peered at the tiny symbols.
revision_level_1.prompt: What does peered mean in this scene?
options: looked closely and carefully
threw the map away
read aloud very quickly
covered the symbols with her hand
accepted_answers: looked closely and carefully
looked closely
tried hard to see

revision_level_2.teaching_block: Practise chapter-word usage by checking whether the word fits the action and object described in the whole sentence.
revision_level_2.passage: The print on a seed catalogue was tiny, so Mrs Ali reached for something that would help her see the letters clearly.
revision_level_2.prompt: Which complete sentence uses spectacles to finish the idea accurately?
options: Mrs Ali put on her spectacles to read the tiny print.
Mrs Ali listened to the catalogue through her spectacles.
Mrs Ali poured her spectacles across the seed page.
Mrs Ali used her spectacles to water the seeds.
accepted_answers: Mrs Ali put on her spectacles to read the tiny print.
she put on her spectacles to read

revision_level_3.teaching_block: Now contrast two looking words in one scene. A glance is brief; a scan moves across several details while searching for one.
revision_level_3.passage: At the station, Nia glanced at the departure time, then scanned the long coach list until she found C7.
revision_level_3.prompt: Use the context to explain how Nia's glance differs from her scan.

concept_slots.description: Explains that glanced is a quick look at the departure time.
any_of: quick look at the departure time
glanced means looked for a moment

concept_slots.description: Explains that scanned means looking across the coach list to find C7.

forbidden_phrases: both actions took a long time

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the action after an unfamiliar word to infer whether the look was brief or continued.
independent_check.passage: Vikram glanced at the bus number, nodded, and continued walking toward the correct stop.
independent_check.prompt: What does glanced mean, and which clue supports that meaning?

concept_slots.description: Defines glanced as a quick or brief look.
Uses Vikram's immediate nod or continued walking as the context clue.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer context reading to a new word. Use both the search pattern and the result to explain its meaning.
transfer_check.passage: Leena scanned the noticeboard from top to bottom until she found her surname in the final column.
transfer_check.prompt: What does scanned mean in this context, and what helped you decide?

concept_slots.description: Explains that scanned means looked over the board carefully to find information.
any_of: looked over the board to find something
searched the noticeboard with her eyes
checked the board from top to bottom

concept_slots.description: Uses finding the surname in the final column as the supporting clue.
any_of: surname was in the final column
the result was finding her surname

levels.title: Retell the search clearly
levels.focus: select and order the main events in a search
levels.teaching_goal: Identify a problem, the useful response, and the result, then summarize them in a sensible order.

guided_check.teaching_block: Sequence words such as first, next, and then help readers track when each event happens.
guided_check.passage: First, Papa read a note. Next, he removed his spectacles to clean them. Then the doorbell rang, and he left them beside the cloth.
guided_check.prompt: What happened immediately before the doorbell rang?
options: Papa removed his spectacles to clean them.
Papa opened the front door.
Papa found the spectacles in a case.
Papa folded the cleaning cloth.
accepted_answers: Papa removed his spectacles to clean them.
he took off his spectacles to clean them
he removed his glasses

bridge.teaching_block: A useful summary keeps the central problem and result while leaving out minor movements.
bridge.passage: Auntie could not find the cupboard key. She retraced her steps from the pantry to the sink and found it beside the soap dish.
bridge.prompt: Which sentence best summarizes the event?
options: Auntie retraced her steps and found the missing key beside the sink.
The pantry and sink were in different rooms.
Auntie washed every dish before opening the cupboard.
The soap dish was a gift from a neighbour.
accepted_answers: Auntie retraced her steps and found the missing key beside the sink.
auntie retraced her steps and found the key

masterclass.teaching_block: A complete one-sentence summary joins the problem, the most useful action, and the result in story order.
masterclass.passage: The family checked shelves and cushions for Papa's spectacles. Tara retraced his steps, noticed the cleaning cloth near the radio, and found the spectacles tucked beneath it.
masterclass.prompt: Summarize the search in one sentence using the problem, Tara's useful action, and the result.

concept_slots.description: Identifies the search for Papa's missing spectacles.
any_of: they could not find the spectacles

concept_slots.description: States that Tara retraced Papa's steps or noticed the cleaning cloth.
any_of: she followed where Papa had been
she checked near the radio cloth

concept_slots.description: Ends with the spectacles being found under the cloth.
any_of: found the spectacles under the cloth
she discovered them near the radio
the search ended under the cleaning cloth

revision_level_1.teaching_block: Rebuild the event order before summarising. Time words help you identify what happened just before or after another action.
revision_level_1.passage: First, Lata packed her paintbrushes. Next, she moved her apron from a chair to the wall hook. Then the art bell rang, and everyone left the room.
revision_level_1.prompt: What did Lata do immediately before the art bell rang?
options: She moved her apron to the wall hook.
She left the room before packing.
She washed every paintbrush.
She took the apron home.
accepted_answers: She moved her apron to the wall hook.
moved her apron to the wall hook
put the apron on the hook

revision_level_2.teaching_block: Next, choose a main-idea sentence that keeps the missing item, the useful retrace, and the discovery while dropping side details.
revision_level_2.passage: Adil could not find his signed permission slip. He remembered showing it to the coach at lunch, returned to the field office, and found that the coach had clipped it inside the team folder.
revision_level_2.prompt: Which sentence is the clearest summary of Adil's search?
options: Adil retraced the permission slip to the field office and found it clipped in the team folder.
Adil ate lunch before visiting a field near school.
The coach owns a folder with a strong metal clip.
A permission slip needs a signature before a trip.
accepted_answers: Adil retraced the permission slip to the field office and found it clipped in the team folder.
Adil went back to the field office and found the slip in the team folder

revision_level_3.teaching_block: Now draft one supported summary. Put the problem first, the useful retracing action second, and the result last.
revision_level_3.passage: The school announcer misplaced her cue card before the afternoon broadcast. She retraced her route to the library, noticed its blue clip near the return desk, and found the card beneath an atlas. She brought it back before the microphone switched on.
revision_level_3.prompt: Write one ordered sentence summarising the problem, the useful action, and the result.

concept_slots.description: States that the announcer's cue card was missing before the broadcast.
any_of: cue card was missing before the broadcast
she could not find the cue card

concept_slots.description: States that she retraced her route to the library or followed the blue-clip clue.
any_of: retraced her route to the library
noticed the blue clip near the return desk

concept_slots.description: Ends with finding the card beneath the atlas and returning before the broadcast.
any_of: brought it back before the broadcast
recovered the card before the microphone switched on
the card was under the atlas

independent_check.teaching_block: Select only the turning points from the new event and keep them in the order they happened.
independent_check.passage: Aman missed his sketchbook at art time. He remembered using it in the courtyard, returned to the stone bench, and found it beneath a folded newspaper.
independent_check.prompt: Write a one-sentence summary of Aman's problem, action, and result.

concept_slots.description: States that Aman could not find or missed his sketchbook.
any_of: Aman could not find his sketchbook
he missed his sketchbook at art time

concept_slots.description: States that he remembered the courtyard and returned to the bench.
any_of: remembered using it in the courtyard
retraced his steps to the courtyard

concept_slots.description: Ends with finding the sketchbook under the newspaper.
any_of: sketchbook was under a folded newspaper

forbidden_phrases: he found it in the classroom

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer problem-action-result summarizing to a non-search event and keep only the details that change the outcome.
transfer_check.passage: A science group's bulb would not glow. The students checked the battery, followed each wire, found a loose clip, and reconnected it. The bulb lit at once.
transfer_check.prompt: Summarize how the group solved the problem in one ordered sentence.

concept_slots.description: Identifies that the bulb would not glow.
States that the group checked the circuit and reconnected the loose clip.
any_of: found and reconnected a loose clip
followed the wires to the loose clip

concept_slots.description: Ends with the bulb lighting.

levels.title: Build precise search sentences
levels.focus: use naming, describing, action, pair, and location words
levels.teaching_goal: Recognize useful word jobs and combine them into complete sentences about objects and locations.

guided_check.teaching_block: A verb tells what someone or something does. In a complete sentence, find the action word first.
guided_check.passage: The curious child lifted the dusty cushion.
options: lifted
curious
child
dusty
accepted_answers: lifted

bridge.teaching_block: Some nouns name objects with two matching parts. Use a pair of before spectacles, shoes, socks, or scissors.
bridge.passage: Papa bought a new pair of ___ for reading fine print.
options: spectacles
ink
paper
sunlight
accepted_answers: spectacles
glasses

masterclass.teaching_block: A precise complete sentence can include a naming word, a describing word, an action, and a location phrase.
masterclass.passage: Sentence facts: object - spectacles; describing word - silver; action - rested; place - beside the lamp.
masterclass.prompt: Turn all four facts into one complete sentence.

concept_slots.description: Uses silver to describe the spectacles.
Uses rested as the action or state.
Places the spectacles beside the lamp.

revision_level_1.teaching_block: Start with one word job. An adjective describes a noun by telling what kind, which one, or how it looks or feels.
revision_level_1.passage: The alert nurse carried the heavy box.
revision_level_1.prompt: Which word is the adjective describing the box?
options: heavy
carried
nurse
the
accepted_answers: heavy

revision_level_2.teaching_block: Next, check that a sentence includes the object, its description, the action, and an exact place without changing the facts.
revision_level_2.passage: Facts: object - compass; describing word - small; action - slipped; place - beneath the open notebook.
revision_level_2.prompt: Which option turns all four facts into a complete sentence?
options: The small compass slipped beneath the open notebook.
The open compass notebook small beneath.
The compass was small, but no action or place is given.
Beneath the compass, the notebook slipped outside.
accepted_answers: The small compass slipped beneath the open notebook.
the small compass slipped beneath the open notebook

revision_level_3.teaching_block: Now build the sentence yourself. Use the describing noun phrase first, follow it with the action, and finish with the location.
revision_level_3.passage: Sentence facts: careful librarian; placed; torn map; inside a clear folder.
revision_level_3.prompt: Combine every fact into one precise complete sentence.

concept_slots.description: Uses careful to describe the librarian.
States that the librarian placed the torn map.
Places the map inside a clear folder.

independent_check.teaching_block: Write a complete sentence from new facts. Include who acted, what was moved, and the location phrase.
independent_check.passage: A careful mechanic placed a pair of gloves beneath a wooden stool.
independent_check.prompt: Rewrite the detail as one complete sentence naming the person, action, object, and place.

concept_slots.description: Names the careful mechanic as the person.
States that the mechanic placed the pair of gloves.
Places the gloves beneath the wooden stool.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer complete-sentence building to a different object. Use the given adjective and an accurate location phrase.
transfer_check.passage: On the craft table, a bright ribbon lay inside a shallow box.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence that describes the ribbon and tells exactly where it was.

concept_slots.description: Uses bright to describe the ribbon.
Places the ribbon inside the shallow box.

levels.title: Write a useful lost-and-found note
levels.focus: summarize evidence in clear complete sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Write a concise lost-and-found message that identifies the object, its location, the next action, and the reason for that action.

guided_check.teaching_block: A useful notice tells what was found, gives an identifying detail, and states where the owner can ask for it.
guided_check.passage: A blue spectacle case marked PK was found near the music room after lunch.
guided_check.prompt: Which complete notice would help the owner most?
options: A blue spectacle case marked PK was found near the music room; ask at the school office.
Something blue was somewhere in school.
Lunch ended before the music class began.
The music room has several empty chairs.
accepted_answers: A blue spectacle case marked PK was found near the music room; ask at the school office.
a blue spectacle case marked PK was found near the music room and is at the office

bridge.teaching_block: Choose details that help the correct owner identify the object; colour, name, mark, and location are stronger than unrelated facts.
bridge.passage: Mili found a water bottle by the stairs. It has a green lid and the name Arif. She took it to the office.
bridge.prompt: Which sentence gives the most useful identifying detail?
options: The bottle has a green lid and the name Arif.
The stairs have twelve steps.
Mili drank water before class.
The office door was open.
accepted_answers: The bottle has a green lid and the name Arif.
green lid and the name Arif

masterclass.teaching_block: A strong two-sentence note summarizes the find, then explains the safe next action without adding invented details.
masterclass.passage: After art club, Veer found a red pencil pouch under the back table. A card inside said Naina. He gave the pouch to the teacher so it would remain safe.
masterclass.prompt: Write a two-sentence notice that summarizes the find and explains Veer's action.

concept_slots.description: Names the red pencil pouch and where it was found.
any_of: red pencil pouch under the back table
pouch was found beneath the back table
Veer found a red pouch after art club
found the pencil pouch under a table

concept_slots.description: Includes Naina's name as the owner clue.
States that Veer gave it to the teacher to keep it safe or return it.
any_of: gave it to the teacher for safety
handed it to the teacher so Naina can collect it
teacher can return it to the owner

revision_level_1.teaching_block: Begin with identification. Keep the details that distinguish the object, such as colour, pattern, initials, or a name.
revision_level_1.passage: An orange scarf with a zigzag border and the initials LS was found outside the dance room.
revision_level_1.prompt: Which detail would help the owner identify this scarf most reliably?
options: It has a zigzag border and the initials LS.
It was found on a school day.
The dance room has a wide door.
Someone walked through the corridor.
accepted_answers: It has a zigzag border and the initials LS.
zigzag border and the initials LS
the initials LS

revision_level_2.teaching_block: Next, pair a safe action with its reason. The notice should direct the owner to a trusted collection point.
revision_level_2.passage: Kunal found a table-tennis bat marked 5A near the practice court. The sports office keeps equipment that pupils misplace.
revision_level_2.prompt: Which sentence gives the safest useful next action and reason?
options: Take the bat to the sports office so its owner can claim it.
Leave the bat at the court so rain can wash it.
Use the bat until someone notices it is missing.
Hide the 5A mark before asking the class.
accepted_answers: Take the bat to the sports office so its owner can claim it.
take it to the sports office for the owner
the sports office can keep it for collection

revision_level_3.teaching_block: Now practise the full note with a scaffold: sentence one identifies the find; sentence two gives the safe action and why it helps.
revision_level_3.passage: After computer club, Imran found a blue USB pouch marked M. Kaur under the third desk. He gave it to the lab assistant because small digital items are kept in a locked drawer until collection.
revision_level_3.prompt: Write a concise two-sentence lost-and-found note using only these facts.
